The Power-Law Approach of the Consumption Function to its Perfect-Foresight Asymptote

The synthesis proof — compactified core, economics-literature fabric, illustrated on HAFiscal's estimated calibrations

July 8, 2026
Status (2026-07-08) — what this document is

This is the synthesis of the four proofs developed in this program — the presentation of record. It combines the compactified boundary-fixed-point core of alt_proof_compactified.md (route γ: the shortest engine, the easiest to understand, and the version that maps directly onto the computational representation), the economics-literature fabric of alt_proof_econlit.md (route α), the computer-science kinship and certification practice of alt_proof_econcs.md (route β), and the complete original chain (stage_A_proof.md, stage_B_proof.md), which remains the only proof of the fine-structure results. This document adds no new mathematical claims: every theorem below is PROVEN and independently refuter-reviewed (six adversarial panels, zero broken theorems), and each proof body is owned by its source document, cited by label. Terminology and notation follow BST wherever the two programs share an object; §2 states the model in full, with each element deep-linked to the published BST draft. The plain-markdown final_proof.md is the canonical text; this MyST version tracks it. Figures are generated by make_final_proof_figures.py (12/12 pre-registered checks).

0. The theorem in plain economics (a reader’s guide)¶

The question. A very wealthy consumer facing labor-income risk behaves almost like a perfect-foresight consumer: income risk is trivial relative to wealth, so the precautionary motive nearly vanishes. How fast does it vanish as wealth grows? That rate matters computationally — every solution algorithm must assume something above its grid top — and theoretically: the buffer-stock canon proves the ratio version of the approach (BST’s limiting MPC bounds) but neither the level nor the rate (§1.3).

The answer in one sentence. Precautionary saving — the shortfall of consumption below the perfect-foresight rule — dies off as a POWER of wealth ((7), proved in §§3–4: Theorem 1, Paragraph) — the same functional family as the Pareto laws economists know from wealth, firm-size, and city-size distributions (Gabaix 1999, 2009, 2016) — with an exponent min⁡(1,q↑)\min(1, \qup)min(1,q↑​) built from patience, returns, and growth ((2)), and (when q↑>1\qup > 1q↑​>1) a level BBB (Theorem 1, (23)) that is nothing more exotic than a growing-perpetuity (Gordon) value.

The asset-pricing reading (the single most useful translation). Subtract the perfect-foresight Euler equation from the true one and what remains is, exactly, an asset-pricing recursion for the shortfall:

shortfall today  =  discount×E⁡[ shortfall tomorrow ]  +  this quarter’s premium\text{shortfall today} \;=\; \text{discount} \times \E[\,\text{shortfall tomorrow}\,] \;+\; \text{this quarter's premium}shortfall today=discount×E[shortfall tomorrow]+this quarter’s premium
(1)

— price equals discounted continuation value plus dividend. (The schematic is made exact in Lemma 5.1, (13); the translation box at the end of §2 spells out the precise discount and premium.) The “asset” is precautionary saving itself — s(m):=cˉ(m)−c(m)s(m) := \bar{c}(m) - c(m)s(m):=cˉ(m)−c(m), consumption’s shortfall below the perfect-foresight rule cˉ\bar{c}cˉ; its “dividend” is this quarter’s Kimball precautionary premium (≈κ‾(ρ+1)σ2/2wˉ\approx \kap(\rho+1)\sigma^2/2\wbar≈κ​(ρ+1)σ2/2wˉ with wˉ\wbarwˉ total wealth (§1.1) — an Arrow–Pratt-type premium: absolute risk over wealth, hence tiny for the rich; (14), §1.4); the discounting per step is 1/R1/\Rcal1/R, with the state drifting down to ÞΓwˉ\ThornG \wbarÞΓ​wˉ (the wealth recursion (12)). Everything in the theorem is bookkeeping on this recursion: the exponent is about which dividends dominate the present value (near ones or far ones), the amplitude BBB is a perpetuity value, and the trichotomy is Gordon-growth’s convergent / r=gr = gr=g / divergent trichotomy.

What is q↑\qupq↑​? (and why min⁡(1,q↑)\min(1, \qup)min(1,q↑​))¶

Two per-quarter log-rates, both familiar:

  • ln⁡R=ln⁡R−ln⁡Γ\ln \Rcal = \ln R - \ln \GammalnR=lnR−lnΓ — the interest-minus-growth gap: how fast discounting compounds along the journey;

  • Λ=ln⁡(1/ÞΓ)\Lambda = \ln(1/\ThornG)Λ=ln(1/ÞΓ​) — the impatience gap: how fast an arbitrarily rich household’s normalized wealth descends toward its buffer-stock target (under GIC, about Λ\LambdaΛ percent per quarter).

Their ratio is the star of the theorem (at ψ≡1\psi\equiv1ψ≡1; in general the root of (8)):

q↑  =  ln⁡RΛ  =  discounting speeddescent speed.\qup \;=\; \frac{\ln \Rcal}{\Lambda} \;=\; \frac{\text{discounting speed}}{\text{descent speed}}.q↑​=ΛlnR​=descent speeddiscounting speed​.
(2)

The intuition. The descent from wealth wˉ\wbarwˉ back to the target takes T(wˉ)≈ln⁡wˉ/ΛT(\wbar) \approx \ln \wbar / \LambdaT(wˉ)≈lnwˉ/Λ quarters — time-to-target is LOGARITHMIC in wealth (made exact by §3.2’s shells and Paragraph's shell-to-wealth conversion). (“The target” is BST’s buffer-stock target m^\hat{m}m^; §6 defines the precise return region around the target that the descent argument uses — the intuition being that bounded shocks confine the recurrent range of wealth to a compact interval around m^\hat{m}m^ with a computable upper edge — and 6.1 How rarely is the tail visited? The dual (Kesten) root, for economists quantifies how rarely it is visited.) Anything discounted exponentially in TIME therefore becomes a power law in WEALTH:

R−T(wˉ)=wˉ−ln⁡R/Λ=wˉ−q↑.\Rcal^{-T(\wbar)} = \wbar^{-\ln \Rcal/\Lambda} = \wbar^{-\qup}.R−T(wˉ)=wˉ−lnR/Λ=wˉ−q↑​.
(3)

A power law in wealth is exponential discounting read on a logarithmic clock. (The same log-clock conversion generates the Pareto tails of the random-growth literature — there applied to cross-sections of cities and firms, here to a single household’s policy function.) So q↑\qupq↑​ answers: by the time the big precautionary action arrives — near the target — how discounted is it, per unit of log-wealth?

  • q↑>1\qup > 1q↑​>1 (discounting beats the descent): faraway dividends are negligible; the shortfall is dominated by the premium collected here and now, which is ∝1/wˉ\propto 1/\wbar∝1/wˉ (Arrow–Pratt). Realized exponent: 1 (Theorem 1).

  • q↑<1\qup < 1q↑​<1 (descent beats discounting): the shortfall is dominated by the large premia awaiting near the target, discounted back. Realized exponent: q↑\qupq↑​ (Paragraph).

  • Hence q=min⁡(1,q↑)q = \min(1, \qup)q=min(1,q↑​): the shortfall is a sum of both components, and the slower-fading one wins asymptotically (Paragraph). And it can never fade faster than 1/wˉ1/\wbar1/wˉ — a prudent consumer is always at least collecting today’s premium (the 1/wˉ1/\wbar1/wˉ floor: the lower bound on the forcing under (13)). The corollary that this floor makes exponential decay impossible is a legacy-motivated aside, developed in the appendix, not in the main line of the theorem.

  • Permanent shocks make the descent NOISY (a random-walk component in log wealth). Noise lets lucky households linger at high wealth, weakening the effective discounting and LOWERING q↑\qupq↑​ below the deterministic ratio (§5, Theorem 2; the general-ψ\psiψ root solves (8)): for the estimated high-school calibration (CAL-HS, §1.1), ln⁡R/Λ=0.43\ln \Rcal/\Lambda = 0.43lnR/Λ=0.43 but q↑=0.38\qup = 0.38q↑​=0.38; at the college patience ceiling the deterministic ratio is ≈14\approx 14≈14, yet q↑=1.47\qup = 1.47q↑​=1.47.

Notation

q↑\qupq↑​ (up-arrow: the upper-wealth end; code and the wider literature write q∗q^{*}q∗, and HARK’s API is unchanged) is the model’s characteristic root; q=min⁡(1,q↑)q = \min(1, \qup)q=min(1,q↑​) is the realized decay exponent; q~\qtildeq~​ denotes a trial exponent in the detection argument of §4; s(m):=cˉ(m)−c(m)s(m) := \bar{c}(m) - c(m)s(m):=cˉ(m)−c(m) is precautionary saving (defined with the gap in §1.1: s(m)=g(wˉ)s(m) = g(\wbar)s(m)=g(wˉ)).

A characteristic root, and a saddle path. Economists solve linear rational-expectations models by finding the characteristic roots and discarding explosive solutions (Blanchard–Kahn). Equation (8) is exactly the characteristic equation of the linearized Euler dynamics in log wealth: the homogeneous solutions of the shortfall recursion are the powers wˉ−q\wbar^{-q}wˉ−q with qqq solving (8), and the exponent-detection theorem of §4 (Paragraph) is the corresponding stability selection — compensate by any wrong exponent and the transformed problem explodes or dies; only min⁡(1,q↑)\min(1, \qup)min(1,q↑​) is the saddle path.

Vocabulary. Where this document says “the estimated HAFiscal calibrations” it means the parameter values estimated by and used in the HAFiscal paper; §1.1 names the three used here (CAL-HS, CAL-CTOP, CAL-CCAP).

1. What is proven, and where it sits in the economics literature¶

1.1 The claim¶

An infinite-horizon consumer with CRRA utility (coefficient ρ\rhoρ) faces the Friedman–Muth income process of the buffer-stock literature: i.i.d. mean-one permanent shocks ψ\psiψ and transitory shocks θ\thetaθ, whose specification includes a zero-income event of probability ℘>0\pZero > 0℘>0 — the atom is part of the maintained income-process assumption (BST, Assumption ass-shocks; §2 states the process in full and records exactly where the atom is load-bearing). Under the buffer-stock conditions — GIC (growth impatience, ÞΓ:=(βR)1/ρ/Γ<1\ThornG := (\beta R)^{1/\rho}/\Gamma < 1ÞΓ​:=(βR)1/ρ/Γ<1, BST’s GIC-Raw on the growth patience factor), RIC (return impatience, ÞR:=(βR)1/ρ/R<1\ThornR := (\beta R)^{1/\rho}/R < 1ÞR​:=(βR)1/ρ/R<1), and FHWC (finite human wealth, R:=R/Γ>1\Rcal := R/\Gamma > 1R:=R/Γ>1) — the normalized consumption function c(m)c(m)c(m) approaches its perfect-foresight asymptote from below:

How to read this figure. Left: the true consumption function and the perfect-foresight line, plotted to high enough wealth (m=5000m = 5000m=5000, where human wealth is ≈3.6%\approx 3.6\%≈3.6% of total) that the two visibly merge — the shaded wedge between them (precautionary saving s=gs = gs=g) is what the theorem is about. A shallower line means prudence fades more slowly with wealth: for CAL-HS (slope -0.38) the precautionary motive remains quantitatively alive far up the wealth ladder, while at the patience ceiling (slope -1) it dies off at the fastest admissible rate.

All computational figures use calibrations estimated in the HAFiscal paper (full provenance in figures/FIGURES.md; discount factors are survival-adjusted, as there): CAL-HS, based on the estimated parameters of a representative high-school-educated household (q↑=0.381\qup = 0.381q↑​=0.381); CAL-CTOP, the most patient college-educated type as estimated (the top of the estimated discount-factor distribution, q↑=0.694\qup = 0.694q↑​=0.694); and CAL-CCAP, the college patience ceiling (q↑=1.474\qup = 1.474q↑​=1.474) — a GIC-cap calibration: its β\betaβ is capped a hair below the boundary at which BST’s raw growth impatience condition (GIC) would fail; at that patience, BST’s Strong Growth Impatience condition (GIC-Mod, §2) — whose failure marks the frontier beyond which an agent is so patient that no target level of wealth exists and wealth grows without bound — has already failed (§6.1). The two estimated calibrations live in the q↑<1\qup<1q↑​<1 regime (exponent q↑\qupq↑​ itself), the patience ceiling in the q↑>1\qup>1q↑​>1 regime (exponent 1). Two clearly-labeled auxiliary calibrations appear only where a regime cannot be exhibited at estimated patience.

1.2 Situating the result: function-approach, not distribution-tail¶

A reader who knows the modern heavy-tails literature in economics should be told immediately what this theorem is not. The celebrated power laws of Toda (2014), Benhabib–Bisin–Zhu (2011, 2015), Stachurski–Toda (2019), Beare–Toda (2022), and Gouin-Bonenfant–Toda (2023) concern the cross-sectional distribution of the level of wealth: Pareto tails of a stationary distribution, with the tail exponent solving a Kesten-type root equation for the forward dynamics. This paper’s object is different in kind: it is the consumption function itself — a policy function, not a distribution — and the claim is that c(m)c(m)c(m) approaches the perfect-foresight solution according to a power-law decay process in the individual decision-maker’s wealth as that wealth goes to infinity.

The distinction is sharp, not cosmetic. In the transitory-only model (ψ≡1\psi \equiv 1ψ≡1, bounded θ\thetaθ) under GIC, the ergodic distribution of wealth has compact support — there is no Pareto tail of any kind, a fact whose econ-packaged form is precisely Stachurski–Toda’s (2019) impossibility theorem. Yet the consumption gap is exactly a power law. Formally, the two literatures’ root equations are Mellin duals: the distributional-tail equation E⁡[(ÞΓ/ψ)ζ]=1\E[(\ThornG/\psi)^\zeta] = 1E[(ÞΓ​/ψ)ζ]=1 may fail to have any root (it does fail at ψ≡1\psi \equiv 1ψ≡1) while the primal equation (8) always has one — the level R>1\Rcal > 1R>1 is what saves it. The full kinship map is alt_proof_econlit.md §6. Section 6.1 How rarely is the tail visited? The dual (Kesten) root, for economists develops the dual root explicitly — with the estimated calibrations’ numbers — for readers meeting it for the first time.

1.4 The forcing is a precautionary premium¶

The engine below runs on a one-step recursion whose inhomogeneous term J(wˉ)J(\wbar)J(wˉ) is, to leading order, κ‾(ρ+1)σ2/(2ÞΓ)⋅wˉ−1\kap(\rho+1)\sigma^2/(2\ThornG) \cdot \wbar^{-1}κ​(ρ+1)σ2/(2ÞΓ​)⋅wˉ−1 — economically, (κ‾\kapκ​ times) the Kimball (1990) equivalent precautionary premium of the coming period’s normalized income noise at wealth scale wˉ\wbarwˉ: the premium form ψK≈η σ2/2\psi_K \approx \eta\,\sigma^2/2ψK​≈ησ2/2 with CRRA relative prudence η⋅c=ρ+1\eta \cdot c = \rho+1η⋅c=ρ+1. Its sign (uncertainty depresses consumption below the PF line) is Leland (1968)/Sandmo (1970); its small-risk quadratic template is Pratt (1964); its consumption interpretation is Drèze–Modigliani (1972).

Precision note (it trips auditors)

Kimball (1990) states the premium form with coefficient ρ+1\rho+1ρ+1; the multiplicative expansion E⁡[u′(c+W)]=u′(c)(1+ρ(ρ+1)2Var⁡(W)/c2+… )\E[u'(c+W)] = u'(c)\bigl(1 + \tfrac{\rho(\rho+1)}{2}\operatorname{Var}(W)/c^2 + \dots\bigr)E[u′(c+W)]=u′(c)(1+2ρ(ρ+1)​Var(W)/c2+…) carries ρ(ρ+1)\rho(\rho+1)ρ(ρ+1), and both appear below — the Taylor constants c2,c2′c_2, c_2'c2​,c2′​ carry ρ(ρ+1)/2\rho(\rho+1)/2ρ(ρ+1)/2 while the envelope algebra reduces the forcing limit to (ρ+1)(\rho+1)(ρ+1). alt_proof_econlit.md §3.2 reconciles the bookkeeping line by line.

2. Model, conditions, and the imported foundations¶

The model in full (each element deep-linked to its anchor in the published BST draft; the statement is BST’s, so a reader can check any piece against the source).

The symbol correspondence. This corpus (and its HARK consumers) writes relative risk aversion as ρ\rhoρ and permanent income growth as Γ\GammaΓ; BST’s published draft writes γ\gammaγ and G\mathcal{G}G for the same objects. Everything else is shared: Þ:=(Rβ)1/ρ\Thorn := (R\beta)^{1/\rho}Þ:=(Rβ)1/ρ (the absolute patience factor), R:=R/Γ\Rcal := R/\GammaR:=R/Γ, κ‾\kapκ​ and κˉ\bar{\kappa}κˉ (the limiting MPC bounds), ℘\pZero℘ (the zero-income probability), ψ\psiψ and θ\thetaθ (permanent and transitory shocks). The target. Under WRIC + FVAC + GIC-Mod there is a unique target m^>0\hat{m} > 0m^>0 with E⁡[m′/m]=1\E[m'/m] = 1E[m′/m]=1 at m^\hat{m}m^ (BST’s buffer-stock-target theorem), computable from the implicit equation (m^−c(m^)) R E⁡[ψ−1]+1=m^(\hat{m} - c(\hat{m}))\,\Rcal\,\E[\psi^{-1}] + 1 = \hat{m}(m^−c(m^))RE[ψ−1]+1=m^. An agent failing GIC-Mod has no target — the precise content behind “GIC-cap” (§1.1); at the ceiling calibration even the mean log-drift is positive, so normalized wealth drifts up without bound (§6.1). Bounded support of the shocks (Assumption ass-shocks) is what makes the return region around m^\hat{m}m^ (§6) a compact interval; BST’s own bounded-support discussion makes the same point — it is what permits the contraction-rate arguments characterizing the stable target to be made globally rather than only asymptotically.

3. The compactified core: infinity as a boundary point¶

(Proof bodies: alt_proof_compactified.md §§1–3, refuter-reviewed with zero broken; labels below are that document’s. One notational bridge: that document writes the trial exponent as sss; here it is q~\qtildeq~​, keeping sss free for precautionary saving.)

3.1 The coordinate, and “assuming the power law in the limit” as a choice of units¶

Map z:=1/wˉz := 1/\wbarz:=1/wˉ. The half-line [wˉ0,∞)[\wbar_0, \infty)[wˉ0​,∞) becomes (0,zˉ](0, \bar{z}](0,zˉ], and infinite wealth becomes the finite boundary point z=0z = 0z=0 — adjoin it. (This is the one-dimensional Poincaré-compactification chart of dynamical systems; Dumortier–Llibre–Artés 2006, ch. 5 — decorative ancestry, no theorem of theirs is consumed.) Then choose units that embed the conjectured power law: the compensated gap

Wq~(z):=wˉq~ g(wˉ),q~=the compensation (trial) exponent.W_{\qtilde}(z) := \wbar^{\qtilde}\, g(\wbar), \qquad \qtilde = \text{the compensation (trial) exponent}.Wq~​​(z):=wˉq~​g(wˉ),q~​=the compensation (trial) exponent.
(18)

“Assume the power law holds in the limit” is thereby demoted from a hypothesis to a choice of coordinates: nothing is assumed — §4’s Theorem II shows the compactified problem itself detects the right exponent. Figure 2 gives the geometry.

How to read this figure. Left: economics. A household richer than its buffer-stock target saves less than income-plus-interest, so its wealth-to-income ratio drifts down about Λ\LambdaΛ percent per quarter (the GIC drift); each rung of the descent yields a precautionary premium proportional to 1/wealth1/\text{wealth}1/wealth. Right: the same journey after the change of variables z=1/wˉz = 1/\wbarz=1/wˉ, which puts “infinitely wealthy” ON the page as the point z=0z = 0z=0 — the way a phase diagram puts a steady state on the page. The arrows show why the argument is not circular: the recursion always maps a point toward the region where the solution is already controlled, so information flows from known territory to the boundary, never from an assumption about the boundary.

Lemma γ2 (boundedness). W1W_1W1​ is bounded on the compactified domain. At q~=q↑\qtilde = \qupq~​=q↑​ the map z↦z/ÞΓz \mapsto z/\ThornGz↦z/ÞΓ​ shifts log wealth by exactly Λ\LambdaΛ, so it leaves unchanged the position within the multiplicative cycle: the fractional part φ={ln⁡wˉ/Λ}\varphi = \{\ln \wbar/\Lambda\}φ={lnwˉ/Λ}. In log wealth the dynamics repeat with period Λ\LambdaΛ, so what matters asymptotically is the position modulo Λ\LambdaΛ — a circle of circumference Λ\LambdaΛ rather than a single boundary point. Wealth levels sharing the same position in the cycle (equal log-wealth modulo Λ\LambdaΛ) form a family that the shell recursion maps to itself; on each such family the recursion neither contracts nor expands (its multiplier is exactly 1) while its forcing fades geometrically. Proven self-contained here: the two-sided envelope converges to a bounded positive limit set (γ-C1), and the period-by-period smoothing of the position-modulo-Λ\LambdaΛ distribution contributed by the continuous part of the shock is geometrically summable (γ-C2). Upgrading to convergence separately at each position of the cycle needs a uniform bound on how much the limit can vary under small shifts of the position (a modulus of continuity in the cycle variable) — GAP-γ-equicont, honestly open for this engine; the sharp statement — wˉq↑g(wˉ)=P({ln⁡wˉ/Λ})+o(1)\wbar^{\qup} g(\wbar) = P(\{\ln \wbar/\Lambda\}) + o(1)wˉq↑​g(wˉ)=P({lnwˉ/Λ})+o(1), with PPP the log-periodic factor — is Theorem A2 of the original chain, imported. Figure 4(c) makes the practical point sharply: at CAL-HS’s estimated patience (Λ=0.0125\Lambda = 0.0125Λ=0.0125) the periodic component provably has no effect at any attainable precision: its total amplitude — the oscillation osc⁡(P):=sup⁡P−inf⁡P\operatorname{osc}(P) := \sup P - \inf Posc(P):=supP−infP of the log-periodic factor — satisfies osc⁡(P)/Pˉ∼e−α/Λ\operatorname{osc}(P)/\bar{P} \sim e^{-\alpha/\Lambda}osc(P)/Pˉ∼e−α/Λ, far below any numerical floor. That is, the boundary circle collapses numerically to a point — which is exactly why a constant-coefficient power-law extrapolant works in the HAFiscal/HARK code; the inset shows the one calibration in the program with a numerically resolved tone (Λ=0.69\Lambda = 0.69Λ=0.69, amplitude ≈8⋅10−4\approx 8\cdot10^{-4}≈8⋅10−4, correlation 0.9999 between the measured wiggle and its predicted position in the cycle) — the honest evidence that the circle is real.

6. The economics of the proof: the journey to the target¶

The path-sum reading (route α) supplies the economic narrative for the same numbers. Iterate (15)–(16) forward: the gap at wealth wˉ\wbarwˉ is the expected present discounted value of the Kimball precautionary premia the household will collect along its buffer-stock journey from wˉ\wbarwˉ down toward the return region around the target m^\hat{m}m^ — the precise object behind the phrase “toward the target”. In BST’s language the destination is the individual target m^\hat{m}m^ (unique under WRIC + FVAC + GIC-Mod per BST’s buffer-stock-target theorem, and computable from BST’s implicit equation (m^−c(m^)) R E⁡[ψ−1]+1=m^(\hat{m} - c(\hat{m}))\,\Rcal\,\E[\psi^{-1}] + 1 = \hat{m}(m^−c(m^))RE[ψ−1]+1=m^) or the pseudo-target mˇ\check{m}mˇ (GIC-Raw). What the unrolled argument itself consumes is only this: a compact wealth interval containing the target, on which the descent’s bookkeeping can stop. Concretely (Stage A), take the wealth levels wˉ≤ζ\wbar \leq \zetawˉ≤ζ with ζ:=C0/(1−ÞΓ)\zeta := C_0/(1-\ThornG)ζ:=C0​/(1−ÞΓ​) — §3.2’s enlargement constant: above ζ\zetaζ the recursion (12) moves strictly down almost surely (wˉ′≤ÞΓwˉ+C0<wˉ\wbar' \leq \ThornG\wbar + C_0 < \wbarwˉ′≤ÞΓ​wˉ+C0​<wˉ), from inside the interval wealth cannot exit upward (ÞΓζ+C0=ζ\ThornG\zeta + C_0 = \zetaÞΓ​ζ+C0​=ζ), the descent from any wˉ\wbarwˉ enters it in ≈ln⁡(wˉ/ζ)/Λ\approx \ln(\wbar/\zeta)/\Lambda≈ln(wˉ/ζ)/Λ quarters, and the target must lie inside (above ζ\zetaζ wealth falls almost surely, contradicting E⁡[m′/m]=1\E[m'/m] = 1E[m′/m]=1 at m^\hat{m}m^). The region is compact because the transitory shock has bounded support — part of the maintained income-process assumption (BST, Assumption ass-shocks; §2): bounded θ\thetaθ, with the sandwich g≤gˉg \leq \bar{g}g≤gˉ​, is what makes the one-step displacement bound C0C_0C0​ — hence the upper edge ζ\zetaζ — finite and computable from the primitives (C0=max⁡(1, θmax⁡−1+Rgˉ)C_0 = \max(1,\, \theta_{\max} - 1 + \Rcal\bar{g})C0​=max(1,θmax​−1+Rgˉ​) works, read off (12)). With unbounded transitory shocks the region is not compact — a single large draw passes any point, no finite C0C_0C0​ exists — and the renewal argument as given needs the bound; the decay theorem itself still holds via the L4′ moment extension, which replaces the compact-interval bookkeeping with moment bounds (6.1 How rarely is the tail visited? The dual (Kesten) root, for economists, item 3). With permanent shocks the interval is entered and re-entered rather than absorbing (6.1 How rarely is the tail visited? The dual (Kesten) root, for economists, item 2 quantifies the excursions above it). The journey picture is exactly Carroll’s (1997) narrative made quantitative. The trichotomy is then where the gap is earned (Figure 6):

  • q↑>1\qup > 1q↑​>1: the first rungs dominate — the gap is priced at the start of the journey, hence the clean B/wˉB/\wbarB/wˉ with the geometric resolvent 1/(RÞΓ−1)1/(\Rcal\ThornG - 1)1/(RÞΓ​−1).

  • q↑=1\qup = 1q↑​=1: every rung contributes equally — T(wˉ)≈ln⁡wˉ/ΛT(\wbar) \approx \ln \wbar/\LambdaT(wˉ)≈lnwˉ/Λ equal premia ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ the ln⁡wˉ\ln \wbarlnwˉ law.

  • q↑<1\qup < 1q↑​<1: the journey’s end dominates — the gap is priced near the target, which is why its fine structure (the periodic factor’s phase) remembers the landing position {ln⁡wˉ/Λ}\{\ln \wbar/\Lambda\}{lnwˉ/Λ}.

Measured on the estimated HAFiscal calibrations (the bookkeeping is the ψ2\psi^2ψ2-tilted Wald chain — step L′(1)\Lfun'(1)L′(1), weight λB\lambda_BλB​ per rung — which the figure build verified is the only unroll-consistent accounting at estimated patience): the journey’s-end/boundary share is 89% for CAL-HS (q↑=0.38\qup = 0.38q↑​=0.38, end-dominated), 50% for CAL-CTOP (q↑=0.69\qup = 0.69q↑​=0.69, the transition), and 2% for the GIC-cap ceiling CAL-CCAP (q↑=1.47\qup = 1.47q↑​=1.47, head-dominated) — with all three per-rung weights λB\lambda_BλB​ within 1% of 1: estimated patience sits close to the resonance knife-edge, which is the deep reason the historical exponential top-of-grid heuristic was locally harmless even though it is asymptotically impossible (Proposition A0, in the appendix).

How to read this figure (the “when is the shortfall earned?” decomposition). Recall the asset-pricing reading: the shortfall a wealthy household exhibits today is the present value of the stream of precautionary premia (“dividends”) it will collect along its descent toward the target. This figure decomposes that present value by when the dividends accrue. The horizontal axis is progress along the descent, rung by rung, rescaled to [0,1][0,1][0,1]: 0 = the first rung — today, at wealth wˉ=105\wbar = 10^5wˉ=105; 1 = the last premium-collecting rung, just above the unroll’s cutoff at wˉ=600\wbar = 600wˉ=600 — well inside the approach to the target but still above the return region around m^\hat{m}m^ (6.1 How rarely is the tail visited? The dual (Kesten) root, for economists quantifies how rarely the lowest rungs are ever visited). The height is that rung’s share of the summed rung values — the plotted shares sum to one — while the terminal boundary term (the continuation value parked at the cutoff) is excluded from the normalization and reported separately in each panel. Three readings:

  • CAL-HS (q↑=0.38\qup = 0.38q↑​=0.38): the mass sits at the right. The shortfall of a wealthy high-school-calibration household is almost entirely the discounted shadow of the future — the intense precautionary saving it anticipates doing near the target. Like a growth stock, its value lives in distant dividends. (Measured: the terminal boundary term alone carries 89% of the total value.)

  • Patience ceiling CAL-CCAP (q↑=1.47\qup = 1.47q↑​=1.47): the mass sits at the left. Discounting beats the descent, so value lives in near dividends, like a coupon bond. (Boundary share: 2%.)

  • Exact resonance (q↑=1\qup = 1q↑​=1): flat. Every quarter of the journey contributes equally — which is exactly why the resonance case picks up the ln⁡wˉ\ln \wbarlnwˉ factor: T≈ln⁡wˉ/ΛT \approx \ln \wbar/\LambdaT≈lnwˉ/Λ equal contributions.

The punchline for HAFiscal: all three estimated-calibration profiles are close to flat, because the estimated economies sit near the r=gr = gr=g knife-edge (§6, the λB\lambda_BλB​-within-1%-of-1 measurement). That single fact is the deepest reason top-of-grid behavior is delicate at realistic patience: the value of the shortfall is spread almost evenly over the whole journey, so no part of the wealth domain is safely negligible.

6.1 How rarely is the tail visited? The dual (Kesten) root, for economists¶

The theorem describes c(m)c(m)c(m) at wealth levels the agent rarely — in one important case never — holds. This subsection quantifies “rarely”, because the correct quantifier is itself an object worth knowing: the tail exponent of a Kesten process. (Evidence for every number below: verify_dualroot_checks.py, ALL PASS, same 7-atom ψ\psiψ discretization as the figures.)

Economists have met this machine under another name: random growth. Multiply a variable by an i.i.d. factor each period (plus a small additive perturbation); if the factor shrinks on average but sometimes exceeds one, the stationary distribution develops a Pareto upper tail whose exponent solves E⁡[factorζ]=1\E[\text{factor}^\zeta] = 1E[factorζ]=1. This is the mechanism behind Zipf’s law for cities — Gabaix (1999) shows that Gibrat-style proportional random growth of city populations, with a small friction keeping cities from vanishing, produces a power-law size distribution, with the Zipf exponent 1 emerging in the small-friction limit — and the standard account of Pareto tails in wealth and firm size. Gabaix (2009) surveys both the empirical catalog (income and wealth, cities, firms, stock returns, trading volume, executive pay) and the generating theory, including precisely the exponent equation E⁡[Aζ]=1\E[A^\zeta] = 1E[Aζ]=1 below; Gabaix (2016) is the introduction written for the general economist, arguing these are true quantitative laws — empirically established and theoretically understood. Everything below is that familiar machine, applied to a single household’s normalized wealth rather than to a cross-section of cities or firms.

Rearranging the master identity (25), normalized wealth follows

wˉ′=A′ wˉ+B′,A′:=ÞΓψ′,B′:=W′+R g(wˉ)ψ′  (bounded: g≤gˉ),\wbar' = A'\, \wbar + B', \qquad A' := \frac{\ThornG}{\psi'}, \qquad B' := \frac{W' + \Rcal\, g(\wbar)}{\psi'} \ \ (\text{bounded: } g \leq \bar{g}),wˉ′=A′wˉ+B′,A′:=ψ′ÞΓ​​,B′:=ψ′W′+Rg(wˉ)​  (bounded: g≤gˉ​),
(28)

a stochastic recursion with i.i.d. multiplier — the workhorse of the wealth-distribution literature (Kesten 1973; Goldie 1991; econ packagings Benhabib–Bisin–Zhu 2011, Toda 2014; the Gouin-Bonenfant–Toda 2023 toolkit’s getZeta computes exactly the object below). The dual (Kesten) root is the unique ζ∗>0\zeta^* > 0ζ∗>0 solving

E⁡[Aζ∗]  =  E⁡[(ÞΓ/ψ)ζ∗]  =  1,\E[A^{\zeta^*}] \;=\; \E\Bigl[\bigl(\ThornG/\psi\bigr)^{\zeta^*}\Bigr] \;=\; 1,E[Aζ∗]=E[(ÞΓ​/ψ)ζ∗]=1,
(29)

which exists precisely when the multiplier (i) contracts on average, E⁡[ln⁡A]<0\E[\ln A] < 0E[lnA]<0, and (ii) occasionally expands, Pr⁡(A>1)>0\Pr(A > 1) > 0Pr(A>1)>0. When it exists, the stationary distribution of wˉ\wbarwˉ has a power tail with exponent ζ∗\zeta^*ζ∗: Pr⁡(wˉ>t)\Pr(\wbar > t)Pr(wˉ>t) decays essentially like t−ζ∗t^{-\zeta^*}t−ζ∗ (the upper bound is an elementary Chernoff/supermartingale estimate; the matching lower bound is the Kesten–Goldie theorem, with the usual non-arithmeticity caveat — a discretized ψ\psiψ technically sits in the lattice case, where Kevei’s 2017 version supplies the log-periodic analogue). Duality made precise: ζ∗\zeta^*ζ∗ and the theorem’s q↑\qupq↑​ solve the two members of one Mellin family — the dual equation (29) governs the tail of the wealth distribution; the primal equation (8) governs the approach of the consumption function. §1.2’s obstruction is the case where the dual root fails to exist while the primal always does.

The reachability taxonomy (answering: with random shocks, what can “unreachable” even mean?):

  1. ψ≡1\psi \equiv 1ψ≡1, bounded θ\thetaθ — literally unreachable. A≡ÞΓ<1A \equiv \ThornG < 1A≡ÞΓ​<1: no expansion, ever; wˉ′≤ÞΓwˉ+C0\wbar' \leq \ThornG \wbar + C_0wˉ′≤ÞΓ​wˉ+C0​ gives an absorbing interval (the return region of §6), so the ergodic support is compact — zero probability beyond a finite point, not merely small. This is the strongest form of §1.2’s contrast: no wealth tail of any kind, yet the gap is exactly a power law.

  2. Permanent shocks, even bounded (the HAFiscal case) — reachable but power-law rare. The 7-atom estimated ψ\psiψ has ψmin⁡=0.9217<ÞΓ\psi_{\min} = 0.9217 < \ThornGψmin​=0.9217<ÞΓ​ at all three calibrations, so Pr⁡(A>1)>0\Pr(A > 1) > 0Pr(A>1)>0: a lucky run of small permanent shocks ratchets normalized wealth up without bound — the support is unbounded even though every shock is bounded. “Behaviorally reachable” is then a measure-and-time statement: tail mass ∼t−ζ∗\sim t^{-\zeta^*}∼t−ζ∗, excursions mean-reverting at rate ∣E⁡[ln⁡A]∣|\E[\ln A]|∣E[lnA]∣ per quarter.

    calibrationE⁡[ln⁡A]\E[\ln A]E[lnA]dual root ζ∗\zeta^*ζ∗Pr⁡(wˉ>10×typical)\Pr(\wbar > 10\times\text{typical})Pr(wˉ>10×typical) (Chernoff scale)
    CAL-HS-0.01139.19∼6⋅10−10\sim 6\cdot10^{-10}∼6⋅10−10
    CAL-CTOP-0.00393.17∼7⋅10−4\sim 7\cdot10^{-4}∼7⋅10−4
    CAL-CCAP (GIC-cap ceiling)+0.0009\mathbf{+0.0009}+0.0009noneno stationary wˉ\wbarwˉ from impatience alone

    Patience fattens the tail (9.2→3.2→9.2 \to 3.2 \to9.2→3.2→ none) — the familiar patience-to-Pareto mechanism of the wealth-distribution literature, here seen from inside a single agent’s problem.

  3. Unbounded θ\thetaθ — any level is possible. One large transitory draw passes any point, so there is no finite maximal wealth at all; the ergodic tail then inherits the income tail (Stachurski–Toda 2019). The theorem is indifferent: the L4′ extension covers unbounded θ\thetaθ.

The patience-ceiling exception. At the GIC-cap ceiling (CAL-CCAP) the mean log-drift is positive: under the reduced i.i.d. dynamics that calibration’s normalized wealth drifts up forever — impatience alone never pulls it back, and no dual root exists. The cap’s construction pins raw growth impatience to hold — barely (ÞΓ=0.99964<1\ThornG = 0.99964 < 1ÞΓ​=0.99964<1) — while the ψ\psiψ-modified conditions fail (E⁡[ln⁡(ÞΓ/ψ)]=+0.0009>0\E[\ln(\ThornG/\psi)] = +0.0009 > 0E[ln(ÞΓ​/ψ)]=+0.0009>0 and E⁡[ÞΓ/ψ]≈1.002>1\E[\ThornG/\psi] \approx 1.002 > 1E[ÞΓ​/ψ]≈1.002>1): the raw, log-drift, and expectation-of-ratio conditions are separated by Jensen gaps, and the ceiling calibration sits between raw and modified — an estimated-parameters instance of BST’s condition-lattice distinctions, the case in which GIC-Mod fails while GIC holds, so only the pseudo-target survives. What truncates that calibration’s ergodic wealth in the full model (the distribution whose extreme upper quantile fixes the top of the estimation grid) is mortality with replacement — the reset mechanism of the wealth-tail literature (Toda 2014) — and within an expected working life its upward drift moves wealth only ≈15%\approx 15\%≈15%.

Practical conclusion, sharpened. The asymptotic region is visited with stationary probability ranging from t−9t^{-9}t−9 (CAL-HS) down to “only via the mortality-reset tail” (CAL-CCAP) — and in the ψ≡1\psi \equiv 1ψ≡1 benchmark, never. The theorem’s practical role is therefore exactly as §7 frames it: a boundary condition and extrapolation form for the function, not a description of states to simulate.

7. The computational payoff: why the compactified core is the right presentation¶

  1. The boundary value is a boundary condition. Solving on a compactified grid z∈[0,zˉ]z \in [0, \bar{z}]z∈[0,zˉ] (equivalently, a top-of-grid asymptotic condition) is standard numerical practice; Theorem I upgrades the practice to principle: the exact boundary data at z=0z = 0z=0 is W(0)=BW(0) = BW(0)=B (q↑>1\qup > 1q↑​>1), i.e. c(m)≈κ‾(m−1+h)−B/mc(m) \approx \kap(m-1+h) - B/mc(m)≈κ​(m−1+h)−B/m at the top of the grid — with BBB known in closed form from the calibration.

  2. The extrapolation form of record. The gap extrapolant g≈C wˉ−q=C (m−1+h)−qg \approx C\,\wbar^{-q} = C\,(m-1+h)^{-q}g≈Cwˉ−q=C(m−1+h)−q, q=min⁡(1,q↑)q = \min(1, \qup)q=min(1,q↑​), is the asymptotically correct form — the theorem behind the decay_extrap='powerlaw' flip in the HAFiscal/HARK code (RECONCILED-002; HARK PR fix-aggshock-pf-decay-extrap), replacing the historical exponential heuristic, which the appendix (Proposition A0) shows is not merely inaccurate but impossible as an asymptotic form.

  3. The knife-edge window, quantified on HAFiscal’s own numbers. At the estimated calibrations the growth patience factor is close to 1 (Λ→0\Lambda \to 0Λ→0) and the asymptotic regime begins only at astronomically large wealth. CAL-CCAP makes this concrete: Λ=3.6⋅10−4\Lambda = 3.6\cdot10^{-4}Λ=3.6⋅10−4, q↑=1.474\qup = 1.474q↑​=1.474, Bψ=357B_\psi = 357Bψ​=357 — and the compensated gap has covered only 42% of the way to its boundary value at the top of the estimation grid, 91% even at 130×130\times130× the grid top (Figure 3a). That is why the exponential heuristic was locally harmless on historical grids (≤0.22%\leq 0.22\%≤0.22% policy effect at the audited window) even though it is asymptotically wrong.

  4. A built-in diagnostic. Theorem γ-T’s detection property is a practical grid test: compensate the measured gap by trial exponents; only min⁡(1,q↑)\min(1, \qup)min(1,q↑​) stabilizes.

  5. The computer-science face. In algorithmic terms the sandwich (15)–(16) is a perturbed divide-and-conquer recurrence, and (8) is its Akra–Bazzi critical-exponent equation ∑iaibip=1\sum_i a_i b_i^{p} = 1∑i​ai​bip​=1 at p=−q↑p = -\qupp=−q↑​; the trichotomy including the resonance log is the master theorem’s three cases (Akra–Bazzi 1998; Leighton 1996). That proof is carried out in full in alt_proof_econcs.md, with hypothesis-match tables against the machine-formalized statements (Isabelle AFP Akra_Bazzi; Lean 4 mathlib4 Computability/AkraBazzi) and executed interval-arithmetic certificates.
